rated_messages.input_message: If you find yourself with a few minutes to spare, it can be nice to read back over old messages. It's also a chance to reply to ones that you might have forgotten about!

Think about a happy memory to ease the difficulty of your urge. Is there something you have been wanting to do for a while that you know you would enjoy? Reading? Walking? Calling a friend? Doing a puzzle? Do something that matters to you instead of smoking.
Urges can feel like stormy weather. But if you're the sky, you just let that storm come and go on it's own knowing that it won't last forever.
Setting small goals when you feel unmotivated is best. Maybe a small goal for now is to breathe deeply for the next 3 minutes instead of smoking.
Each time you choose to not smoke after seeing someone else light up, you lessen the habit a little more.
Even though you are stressed, are you willing to sit with this urge until it passes if will help you break this habit?
What inspires you most to quit smoking? Are you willing to let this urge pass without smoking for that reason?

Imagine your urge is like a talk radio station going on about something you disagree with. Arguing with it doesn't change what they say. Instead, just let them talk while you focus on what's important to you.
If you have trouble resisting a craving when other smokers are around, try carrying a water bottle and taking a sip every time you want to ask for a cig.
